parole.significato: The practice of living diligently with an organized daily routine.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 갓생 (gatsaeng), from English God + 생 (saeng, “life”), the latter from Middle Chinese 生 (MC sraeng|sraengH).

parole.significato: Sorrowful resentment, as a part of the Korean cultural identity.
parole.testo: From Korean 한(恨) (han), from Middle Chinese 恨 (MC honH).

parole.significato: The Han character script used to write Korean, particularly in classical literature.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 한자(漢字) (hanja), from Middle Chinese 漢字 (MC xanH dziH, “Chinese character”, literally “Han Chinese + character”). Compare Cantonese 漢字 /汉字 (hon³ zi⁶), Japanese 漢字 (kanji), Mandarin 漢字 /汉字 (hànzì), Vietnamese Hán tự. Doublet of kanji and Hanzi.

parole.testo: Borrowed from kwūkyel, the Yale romanization of Korean 구결(口訣) (gugyeol), from Middle Chinese 口訣 (MC khuwX kwet, “mnemonic rhyme”), from 口 (kǒu, “mouth”) + 訣 /诀 (jué, “rhymed saying”).

parole.significato: In South Korea, peasants or working-class people.
parole.testo: From Korean 민중(民衆) (minjung), from Middle Chinese 民眾 (MC mjin tsyuwngH, “common people, the masses”). Compare Mandarin 民眾 /民众 (mínzhòng).
